candidates.change_summary: Change the return value from ERC721TokenReceiver.onERC721Received.selector to bytes4(0) so the returned success value differs.
Replace the assignment 'baseToken = _baseToken;' with 'baseToken = address(0);' so that baseToken is always zero after initialization.
Replace the assignment 'baseToken = _baseToken;' with 'baseToken = _nft;' so that baseToken is set to the NFT address instead.
Insert 'baseToken = _nft;' after the existing assignment to overwrite baseToken with the NFT address.
Delete the statement 'baseToken = _baseToken;' so baseToken remains its default value of address(0).

Move 'baseToken = _baseToken;' after 'nft = _nft;' is not possible because it would only swap lines with no semantic effect. Instead, move 'baseToken = _baseToken;' to after 'initialized = true;' so the state variable is set, but after the initialization flag is already true, potentially allowing re-entrancy to see an intermediate state where baseToken is still zero.
Assign a different address (e.g. msg.sender) to nft instead of the passed _nft parameter.
Delete the assignment nft = _nft so nft retains its default zero address.
Assign baseToken to nft instead of _nft, causing nft to equal the base token address.
Move the nft = _nft assignment to before the initialized check, causing it to execute even if the contract is already initialized, which could overwrite a previously set value with _nft.
Replace the assignment to changeFee with a constant zero so initialize stores a different value.
Move the changeFee assignment after feeRate assignment so it takes the value of feeRate instead of _changeFee.
Delete the fee rate assignment so feeRate retains its default zero instead of the passed value.
Delete the fee rate upper-bound check so an arbitrary high value can be stored.
Replace feeRate = _feeRate with feeRate = _feeRate + 1, storing a different value.
Delete the assignment `initialized = true;` so that the contract remains uninitialized after the call.
Replace `payRoyalties = _payRoyalties;` with `payRoyalties = !_payRoyalties;` so the stored value is the negation of the parameter.
Replace `payRoyalties = _payRoyalties;` with `payRoyalties = true;` so royalties are always enabled regardless of the parameter.
Replace `payRoyalties = _payRoyalties;` with `payRoyalties = false;` so royalties are never enabled regardless of the parameter.
Delete the statement `payRoyalties = _payRoyalties;` so `payRoyalties` keeps its default value (false).
